clue.text: Pen a note: check boxes measuring small dimensions

indicators.note: a thing that boxes another holds it inside, so the preceding words contain the solution

blocks.note: the letters run on across the word breaks, ignoring the colon

explanation.surface: Someone writes a quick memo and ticks boxes on a form about tiny measurements.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon breaks the surface into instructions, but the punctuation is ignored: the run starts at the last letter of Pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanotechnology works at the scale of billionths of a metre, so it deals in minute sizes.

clue.text: European misses out on a new beginning

indicators.note: missing out on something means going without it, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: a German is a European
A taken as written, N the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A European fails to get a fresh start in life.
explanation.walkthrough: GERMAN loses its final AN, leaving GERM.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ is the seed or first origin from which something grows, as in the germ of an idea.

clue.text: Be undecided about one claim forgone

indicators.note: about here means around, so the first word is wrapped round the other

blocks.note: to waver is to hesitate between choices
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone dithers over giving up a claim they once made.
explanation.definitionFit: A waiver is the formal act of relinquishing a right, so it is a claim surrendered voluntarily.

clue.text: I make careless mistake in feeble poem, after change of heart

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the following word

blocks.note: pale in the sense of weak, as in a pale imitation
taken as written
to nod is to slip up through inattention, as even Homer nods

explanation.surface: A poet confesses to a sloppy slip in a weak poem, having had second thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: To nod is the old idiom for a lapse of attention, as in 'even Homer nods'.
explanation.definitionFit: A palinode is an ode in which the poet retracts views expressed in an earlier piece of verse.

clue.text: More than one firm Tory type rejecting Heath from tedium

indicators.note: rejecting something means throwing it out, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: Con is short for Conservative
a type is a sort or kind
Ted Heath was a Conservative prime minister of the 1970s
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Conservative type turns away from Edward Heath's dullness.
explanation.walkthrough: TEDIUM loses TED, leaving IUM to end the word; Edward Heath was widely called Ted.
explanation.definitionFit: A consortium is an association of several companies working together on a joint venture.

clue.text: Sympathised with one sort of public house under pressure

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under something places it after, lower in the column

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure
the Roman numeral for one
a tied house is a British pub bound to sell one brewery's beer

explanation.surface: Someone felt sorry for a pub under financial strain.
explanation.definitionFit: To pity someone is to feel compassion for their suffering, so pitied is felt sorry for.

clue.text: Bawdy author's first mob, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the words are to be heard, not spelt

blocks.note: a mob is a rabble, and first is A, as in grade A

explanation.surface: A ribald writer's earliest gang, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, rabble-A comes out like the French writer's name; the 's is read as 'is' joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: François Rabelais, creator of Gargantua and Pantagruel, is famous for coarse, earthy comic writing.

clue.text: In predicament, fight with energy

blocks.note: a scrap is a scuffle
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone in a tight spot fights back vigorously.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a scrape is to be in an awkward or troublesome situation of one's own making.

clue.text: Kind of kitten or cat, one included in bill

indicators.note: what is included in something sits inside it

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat
the Roman numeral for one
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A question of which young or adult cat appears on an invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: Atomic Kitten was a British girl group of the early 2000s, which is what makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The pop band name Atomic Kitten makes atomic the particular sort of kitten wanted here.

clue.text: Appear vaguely in room, where one goes mad unnoticed

indicators.note: notice can be an advert, so un-noticed means the advert is taken away

blocks.note: a loo is the toilet, the room one goes to
taken as written
an ad is a notice, which is removed

explanation.surface: A dim shape materialises in a room where someone quietly goes insane.
explanation.walkthrough: A notice in the sense of an advertisement is what gets removed; loo is British for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To loom is to come into view as a shadowy, indistinct and often threatening shape.

clue.text: Part of Atlantic's valuable reserve that's not yet exploited

blocks.note: Virgin Atlantic is the airline, so Virgin is part of its name
taken as written
oil reserves are valuable deposits

explanation.surface: Part of the Atlantic holds valuable oil reserves still untapped.
explanation.walkthrough: Atlantic is not the ocean but the airline Virgin Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgin soil is land never ploughed or cultivated, figuratively any field still untouched by development.

clue.text: Flowers return, fed with nitrogen, I detect

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word is read from end to start
something fed with a thing takes it inside

blocks.note: roses are flowers
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Flowers come back after being given nitrogen fertiliser, and I notice.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer speaking: a sensor could say 'I detect' of itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensor is a device whose function is detection, so it could describe itself that way.

clue.text: Top-class con man?

blocks.note: first meaning: excellent, terrific
second meaning, whimsical: an extremely good deceiver, one who tricks people superbly

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading: a duper is one who dupes, and a super one is a champion swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: The reduplicated slang expression means marvellous, and split it suggests an outstanding trickster.

clue.text: Be proud of rhubarb that Mrs Grundy's bottled

indicators.note: what is bottled is held inside a container

blocks.note: rhubarb is British slang for nonsense, as is rot
Mrs Grundy is a stock figure of narrow-minded propriety

explanation.surface: A strait-laced lady is pleased with the rhubarb she has preserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proud' is the misdirection: here it means sticking out, as a nail stands proud of a board.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing proud of a surface means projecting beyond it, which is exactly sticking out.

clue.text: Two blokes meeting pedlar

blocks.note: a chap and a man, two words for a bloke

explanation.surface: Two men run into a travelling salesman.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAP and MAN are the two blokes; bloke is British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapman was an itinerant dealer in small goods, an old word for a hawker.

clue.text: Very inaccurate shot (where one saw it coming?)

blocks.note: first meaning: a shot that misses badly
second meaning, playful: the distance from which something obvious is spotted, as in seeing it from afar

explanation.walkthrough: The bracket gives a joke second reading: you could see something coming from a great distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Missing by a mile is a hugely wide miss, and spotting something from far away is the idiom.

clue.text: What is in Washington? Start to explore and gape

indicators.note: in places the first words inside the city
the start of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: eh is a request to repeat, like what?
taken as written
Washington DC, the US capital
the first letter of explore

explanation.surface: A visitor asks what Washington is like, starts exploring and stares open-mouthed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What is' reads as a question about the city, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically, to dehisce is for a seed pod or fruit to split open, so it yawns apart.

clue.text: Vineyard Frenchwoman runs with less compassion

blocks.note: a cru is a French wine-growing estate
elle is French for she
R for runs in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A French vineyard owner runs her business more heartlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Crueller is the comparative of cruel, meaning showing more heartlessness toward others.

clue.text: Some roofs are abused

blocks.note: first meaning: covered with slates
second meaning: harshly criticised

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests mistreated roofs, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Roofs may be tiled with slate, and a critic who slates a play attacks it verbally.

clue.text: He led miners from cliff to ravine

blocks.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff
a gill (or ghyll) is a narrow ravine in northern England

explanation.surface: A leader takes miners across rugged country from crag to gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Scargill led Britain's National Union of Mineworkers through the 1984-85 strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Scargill was president of the British mineworkers' union, so he was the miners' leader.

clue.text: Church oversees exam for singers

indicators.note: in a down entry, what oversees another sits above it, so comes first

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: The church supervises a test for its choir.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral describes music written for a choir, a group of vocalists performing together.

clue.text: I have no leisure — almost behind, for example, in verse

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

blocks.note: someone with no free time says they are busy

explanation.surface: A busy person complains of having no spare time and running late.
explanation.walkthrough: I AM BUSY loses its last letter. 'Behind' wants to mean late; it is an example word, stressed be-HIND.
explanation.definitionFit: An iambus is a metrical foot of an unstressed then a stressed syllable, and the word behind has that pattern.

clue.text: According to judges, sons are not consanguineous

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun: relatives who are not blood kin

blocks.note: what judges decide is so in law
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Courts rule that the sons are not related by blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Relatives by marriage, such as a spouse's parents, share no common ancestry with you.

clue.text: Huge old quantity halved in a sort of arithmetic

indicators.note: halved means cut in two, so only the first half is kept
in places the first pieces inside the following word

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a number is a quantity
mental arithmetic is done in the head

explanation.surface: An enormous historical amount gets split in a head-calculation.
explanation.walkthrough: Mental arithmetic is sums done in the head; only the first half of the quantity is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Monumental means on the scale of a monument, so enormous or colossal in size.

clue.text: Lied about being unemployed

indicators.note: about suggests moving round and round, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone was untruthful about being out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can mean without a job or occupation, as with workers laid off.

clue.text: King cobra kills every other Russian

indicators.note: killing every other letter removes alternate ones, keeping the rest

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A deadly snake slays every second Russian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King cobra' looks like the killer of the surface; it is just the source of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor is a typical Russian man's first name, so it stands for a Russian.

clue.text: For delivery to a force to be reckoned with

indicators.note: reckoned means worked out, so these letters must be worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A parcel is addressed to a formidable power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A force to be reckoned with' reads as a stock phrase; it splits into the letters and the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Care of, written c/o on envelopes, means the letter goes via another person's address.

clue.text: Keeping wife and Jack working, makes index

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it, so these pieces go inside

blocks.note: does in the sense of makes or performs
W is the abbreviation for wife
J for jack in a pack of cards
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Supporting his wife and son Jack in employment makes someone a leading indicator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes' looks like part of the surface verb but supplies the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dow Jones Industrial Average is a stock market index tracking major American companies.
